### Task 31: Live certification

> **CHECK-DESIGN RULE — read before writing or editing any check in this task.**
>
> **A check that derives its scope from ONE of the inputs the real job reads will pass while the job does something the check never looked at.** The check stays internally consistent and the gap is invisible from inside it, which is why this keeps recurring: it has produced **five** findings in this plan's reviews so far —
> - r15-02: the FK gate surveyed children of `hcp_profiles`, the one parent under discussion; the cleanup deletes from five, and four of the other parents' rules are CASCADE.
> - r15-04: the content hash assumed the beats touch only D1/D2; the 174 h arrival window keeps the previous real batch eligible.
> - r16-04: check 2b's preview span came from trigger arrival; the territory beat also selects on `bm.created_at`.
> - Step 1c ×2: the territory date assertion and the preview span were both driven by the per-HCP beat's trigger-derived dates. (A third site in the same step, the territory conservation check, had it too.)
> - **Known and deliberately left, 2026-09-15:** `feast_online_check.py` covers `hcp_conversion_features` only, while Step 1d's cleanup touches ten views. It is consumed by Task 30 Steps 3/3b and `publish_cert.sh validate()`, so widening it changes three other gates and is a separate decision. Step 1d adds `cleanup_online_absence.py` over all ten instead of altering the shared script. **This is a recorded decision, not an oversight** — do not "fix" the shared script without re-deciding those three consumers.
>
> **Before adding a check, write down every input the job it verifies actually reads, then derive the check's scope from ALL of them.** Two corollaries learned the hard way:
> - *Do not consistency-fix a check that is correctly single-input.* `PER_HCP_DATES` in Step 1c is trigger-derived because the per-HCP selector genuinely is trigger arrival. Widening it would assert over dates that beat never selected.
> - *Where the scope is a set, save the set, not its span* — and assert coverage (`…_span_uncovered.txt` must be `0`), so a future input silently outside the range fails loudly instead of passing quietly.
> - *An instruction that names a symbol is a claim about the code, and earns a `grep -rn` before it ships* (codex r18-03, r19-02). Twice this plan told an implementer to patch a seam that does not exist — `_kpi_engine_value` (0 hits repo-wide; the real seam is `src.api.routes.kpi.get_kpi_calculator`, imported inside `_kpi_lookup_evidence`) — and once told them to delete a name the test module imports, so the control failed COLLECTION and neither its green cases nor its red ones ever ran. Both were written from memory rather than from the file, and one `grep -rn` would have caught each. **Same family as the heredoc rule: a procedure that cannot run is not a procedure**, whether the cause is a shell redirect eating the script or a symbol that was never there. It is the cheapest check in this lane and it guards the instructions, which nothing else does.
> - *When a predicate is removed from an OPERATION, its mirror in the VERIFICATION of that operation must go with it* (codex r18-01). Otherwise the check now certifies the design you just replaced, and it fails precisely when the new design works. Twice in this plan a migration left its mirror behind: r17-01 (the preflight gate still demanding empty dates after the readout stopped requiring them) and r18-01 (the residue count still demanding zero territory rows on the planted dates after the DELETE stopped removing them) — in the r18-01 case the removal comment and the surviving mirror sat fifty lines apart in the same step. **Grep the removed predicate's own wording across the whole document before reporting the change done**, and read every assertion that names the operation you changed.
> - *And derive the scope from the state AFTER the operation, not before it* (codex r17-02). "Derived from one of the selectors" has a sibling: **derived from the state before the operation**. Check 2b originally proved idempotence over the dates the beats selected BEFORE the plant — but the plant is what makes the planted dates selectable, and planted arrivals reach further still through the 30-day lookback. The scope was right about which selectors exist and wrong about WHEN it sampled them, which passes for the same reason as the source-scoped version: the check is internally consistent and blind in one dimension. Ask what the operation will CAUSE to be in scope, not what is in scope now.
>
> **SEVENTH INSTANCE, same shape from a different direction — a CHECKER whose scope is narrower than what it certifies.** While verifying the Option A edits, a compile pass over this plan's embedded scripts matched ONE heredoc while a plain `grep -c` for the same opening token found TWO. The unmatched one was a real bug: a command carrying BOTH a heredoc and a stdin redirect (`python - <<TAG < some.json`), where **the later redirect wins**, so Python reads the JSON as its script and dies with an error pointing nowhere near the cause. Proved rather than reasoned — redirecting a text file into such a command raises `NameError` on the file's first word. Fixed by passing the path as `sys.argv[1]` instead.
>
> **The transferable part is the detection, not the bug: a heredoc the checker cannot find is a heredoc nobody has checked.** So any check that verifies embedded scripts must first compare the number of scripts it FOUND against the number PRESENT — count the opening tokens with `grep -c`, count the blocks the extractor matched, and fail when they differ. A regex that requires the opening token to be immediately followed by a newline silently skips every block whose command has arguments after the token, which is exactly the shape the bug took.
>
> Note the shape: this is the one-selector rule again, with the *checker's* scope narrower than the artifact's — so the discipline applies to the tools that verify this plan just as much as to the checks inside it. **Do not paste a worked example of this check into the plan**: an example containing the opening tokens is itself counted by the checker, which inflates the "present" count and breaks the very comparison it demonstrates. (Learned immediately: the first draft of this paragraph did exactly that.)

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the cert script** (`$EVID/cert_trx_canonical.py`, untracked evidence)

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Canonical TRx lane post-deploy certification: container, live DB, live API, Feast, chat.

Usage: cert_trx_canonical.py <expected_main_sha> <evidence_dir>
Prints ok/BAD per check; exit 1 if any BAD.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from datetime import date, timedelta

EXPECTED_SHA, OUT = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
MAIN = os.environ.get("E2I_MAIN", os.path.expanduser("~/Projects/e2i_causal_analytics"))
API = os.environ.get("E2I_API_BASE", "https://eznomics.site/api")
ok = bad = 0


def check(name: str, cond: bool, detail: object = "") -> None:
    global ok, bad
    ok += bool(cond)
    bad += not cond
    print(f"[{'ok ' if cond else 'BAD'}] {name}" + (f" — {detail}" if detail != "" else ""), flush=True)


def sh(cmd: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300).stdout.strip()


def psql(sql: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(
        ["docker", "exec", "supabase-db", "psql", "-U", "postgres", "-d", "postgres", "-tA", "-c", sql],
        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120,
    ).stdout.strip()


def env() -> dict:
    d = {}
    for line in open(f"{MAIN}/.env", encoding="utf-8"):
        line = line.strip()
        if line and not line.startswith("#") and "=" in line:
            k, v = line.split("=", 1)
            d[k] = v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    return d


def http(method, url, token=None, body=None, timeout=300, extra=None):
    data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method)
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    if token:
        req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {token}")
    for k, v in (extra or {}).items():
        req.add_header(k, v)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
            return r.status, json.loads(r.read().decode() or "null")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        try:
            return e.code, json.loads(e.read().decode() or "null")
        except Exception:
            return e.code, None

- [ ] **Step 1a: Plant the certification batch** (owner decision #5, 2026-09-15: an authorised production write; this is the DEFAULT path)

Why: the arrival-selected rollups only produce rows when triggers ARRIVE. Waiting for the real Monday batch would hold certification for up to ~7 days, so the owner authorised a labelled planted batch instead.

Scope of the authorisation:
- It covers THIS step's writes and the Step 1d cleanup only.
- Everything before the merge stays read-only, and the Task 30 backfills keep their own GO #1 / GO #2.
- **The reseed cron stays HELD** (Step 5 restores it after CERTIFIED), so nothing else writes triggers during the proof.

**Owner decision #7 (2026-09-15): the plant is a SELF-CONTAINED ENTITY SET.** Every entity the loops touch is itself new and prefixed — its own territory, two HCP profiles, two patients, two journeys and their triggers — so the rollups compute over planted rows only.
- The new territory's market_share denominator contains only its planted HCP, so no real territory's shares move.
- Two HCPs, one per planted date, because `DISTINCT ON (hcp_id, hcp_brand_id)` keeps one row per entity: a single HCP on two dates would sample as ONE weekday and could never satisfy the `weekdays >= 2` gate (codex r13-01).
- Cleanup is exact deletes by prefix, not a whole-table restore (Step 1d).

Rules the proof must satisfy:
- Only rows whose ids start with `certproof_trx_canonical_`, except the one stated exception below.
- The rows must be picked up by the SCHEDULED loops: no manual ETL invocation and no manual materialize between planting and the Step 1b/1c checks.
- Record that a plant happened, independently of which proof path is later chosen (codex r13-04).

**What the 03:45 run does to real territories, stated plainly** (rewritten for owner decision #9). `territory_dates` cross-joins EVERY territory with each selected date, so the run touches a row for each real territory on the planted dates. Under Option A those rows **already exist** and are **recomputed identically** — check 2b proves the recompute is content-preserving, and it is byte-exact because `territory_metrics` has no `updated_at` and no update trigger, and the `ON CONFLICT` SET arm never touches `created_at`. So no real territory row is created or changed; the only NEW row is the planted territory's own, which Step 1d deletes by prefix.

This is the inversion of the earlier design, where the planted dates were empty and each real territory got a NEW zero row that had to be deleted by date and its online key refreshed. Both of those follow-ons are gone: the date-scoped delete would now destroy real rows (part (3) is prefix-only), and the online refresh is unnecessary because the planted rows are never the newest.

**Preflight — all read-only, all must hold before any write.**

```bash
q() { docker exec supabase-db psql -U postgres -d postgres -Atc "$1"; }
# 1. Two candidate dates (OWNER DECISION #9, Option A). They are inside the 7-day TTL and on
#    two distinct weekdays. They are NOT required to be empty — that requirement was dropped
#    because it cannot be met: triggers cover 1,142 of 1,143 calendar days (one gap, 2023-08-04,
#    three years back and far outside the TTL), so `trig = 0` is structurally unreachable in the
#    past, and Task 30 Step 3b's backfill then populates per_hcp and terr for every date with
#    triggers. What the old predicate was really protecting is that the whole-date recompute
#    must not leave rows this cert cannot clean up; decision #7's entity disjointness and check
#    2b's idempotence provide that instead, and this readout now reports rather than gates.
#    BOTH dates must be <= the newest real territory metric_date, so the planted rows are never
#    the newest. The preservation claim itself rests on SOURCE INVARIANCE, not on Redis's skip
#    guard (codex r19-01): no real territory's online entry serves a value differing from its own
#    newest source row. An entry may APPEAR where none existed; that is not a failure. See the
#    premise paragraph in the note where part (4) used to be.
q "SELECT d::date, extract(isodow FROM d) AS dow,
          (SELECT count(*) FROM triggers t WHERE DATE(t.trigger_timestamp) = d::date) AS trig,
          (SELECT count(*) FROM business_metrics b WHERE b.metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup' AND b.metric_date = d::date) AS per_hcp,
          (SELECT count(*) FROM territory_metrics m WHERE m.metric_date = d::date) AS terr,
          (d::date <= (SELECT max(metric_date) FROM territory_metrics)) AS not_newest
     FROM generate_series(CURRENT_DATE - 6, CURRENT_DATE - 1, '1 day') d ORDER BY 1" | tee "$EVID/cert_batch_preflight_dates.txt"
q "SELECT 'newest_territory_metric_date=' || max(metric_date) FROM territory_metrics" | tee -a "$EVID/cert_batch_preflight_dates.txt"
# 2. FK feasibility — GENERATED from the live catalog, for EVERY parent the cleanup deletes.
#    codex r15-02. This is the third time a hand-written FK list has been wrong, so it is no
#    longer hand-written. The earlier version surveyed children of `hcp_profiles` only, because
#    that was the parent under discussion; the cleanup also deletes from `triggers`,
#    `patient_journeys`, `business_metrics` and `territory_metrics`, and those carry NINE more
#    incoming FKs of which FOUR are CASCADE. A CASCADE child is deleted silently BEFORE the
#    hcp_profiles guard ever runs, and neither the five-table content hashes nor the prefix
#    residue checks look at those tables at all.
#    Read from pg_constraint, i.e. the DEPLOYED rules — a migration file can be edited, applied
#    partially, or superseded; `confdeltype` is what Postgres will actually do tonight.
q "WITH RECURSIVE deleted(tbl) AS (
       SELECT unnest(ARRAY['triggers','business_metrics','territory_metrics','patient_journeys','hcp_profiles'])
       UNION
       -- a CASCADE child of a deleted table is itself deleted, so ITS children matter too
       SELECT c.conrelid::regclass::text
         FROM pg_constraint c JOIN deleted d ON c.confrelid = d.tbl::regclass
        WHERE c.contype = 'f' AND c.confdeltype = 'c'
   )
   SELECT d.tbl || ' <- ' || c.conrelid::regclass::text || '.' || a.attname || ' : ' ||
          CASE c.confdeltype WHEN 'a' THEN 'NO ACTION' WHEN 'r' THEN 'RESTRICT'
                             WHEN 'c' THEN 'CASCADE'   WHEN 'n' THEN 'SET NULL'
                             WHEN 'd' THEN 'SET DEFAULT' END
     FROM deleted d
     JOIN pg_constraint c ON c.confrelid = d.tbl::regclass AND c.contype = 'f'
     JOIN unnest(c.conkey) WITH ORDINALITY k(attnum, ord) ON true
     JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = c.conrelid AND a.attnum = k.attnum
    ORDER BY 1" | tee "$EVID/cert_batch_preflight_fks.txt"
wc -l "$EVID/cert_batch_preflight_fks.txt"
grep -c 'CASCADE' "$EVID/cert_batch_preflight_fks.txt"
q "SELECT unnest(enum_range(NULL::region_type))::text" | head -4
q "SELECT unnest(enum_range(NULL::brand_type))::text" | head -4
q "SELECT table_name, column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND column_name = 'territory_id'" | tee "$EVID/cert_batch_preflight_territory_refs.txt"
# 2b. The dates the scheduled beats will actually select during the proof window, and proof
#     codex r17-02: the union below must be PROSPECTIVE, not pre-plant. The plant is what makes
#     D1/D2 selectable, and the planted arrivals additionally reach territory dates across
#     [D, D+30] through the 30-day active-HCP lookback. Deriving the union from the state BEFORE
#     the plant therefore omits exactly the dates the plant causes the beats to touch — a stale
#     real aggregate on one of those uncovered dates passes this preflight, changes during the
#     beat, and survives the prefix-only cleanup. So CHOOSE D1/D2 FIRST (check 1), then add them
#     and their territory reach to the union before proving idempotence over it.
#     This is the one-selector shape in TIME rather than in source: the scope was right about
#     which selectors exist and wrong about WHEN it sampled them.
#     that recomputing them changes nothing (codex r15-04). Holding the cron stops new
#     arrivals; it does NOT make the 174 h arrival window forget the last weekly batch, and the
#     territory variant reaches further still via the 30-day active-HCP lookback. Enumerate,
#     then prove idempotence — do not assert a narrower blast radius than the code has.
#     codex r16-04: BOTH selector date sets go into one reusable CTE, and the preview span is
#     derived from their UNION. Deriving it from triggers alone (the earlier version) misses a
#     date the territory beat reaches through its OTHER branch: a per_hcp_rollup row created
#     recently for an OLDER metric_date — e.g. anything Task 30 Step 3b's backfill wrote — is
#     selected by `bm.created_at` while its triggers sit outside the 174 h arrival window. The
#     preview then reported zero changes for a date the beat will in fact recompute, and the
#     baseline was captured on an idempotence proof with a hole in it.
BEAT_DATES_SQL="
WITH per_hcp AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT DATE(t.trigger_timestamp) AS d
      FROM triggers t
     WHERE t.created_at >= now() - INTERVAL '174 hours' AND t.hcp_id IS NOT NULL
), territory AS (
    -- branch 1: a rollup row WRITTEN in the window, whatever date it belongs to
    SELECT DISTINCT bm.metric_date AS d FROM business_metrics bm
     WHERE bm.metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup' AND bm.created_at >= now() - INTERVAL '174 hours'
    UNION
    -- branch 2: a date whose 30-day active-HCP lookback reaches an arrived trigger
    SELECT DISTINCT bm.metric_date FROM business_metrics bm
     WHERE bm.metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup'
       AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM triggers t
                    WHERE t.created_at >= now() - INTERVAL '174 hours'
                      AND t.trigger_timestamp >= bm.metric_date - INTERVAL '30 days'
                      AND t.trigger_timestamp <  bm.metric_date + INTERVAL '1 day')
), planted AS (
    -- codex r17-02: the dates the PLANT will make selectable. D1/D2 are chosen in check 1 and
    -- exported before this runs; the territory beat additionally reaches any date whose 30-day
    -- active-HCP lookback covers a planted trigger, i.e. [D, D+30].
    SELECT '${D1}'::date AS d
    UNION SELECT '${D2}'::date
    UNION SELECT bm.metric_date FROM business_metrics bm
     WHERE bm.metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup'
       AND (bm.metric_date BETWEEN '${D1}'::date AND '${D1}'::date + 30
         OR bm.metric_date BETWEEN '${D2}'::date AND '${D2}'::date + 30)
), all_dates AS (
    SELECT d FROM per_hcp UNION SELECT d FROM territory UNION SELECT d FROM planted
)
"
q "${BEAT_DATES_SQL} SELECT 'per_hcp_dates|' || count(*) || '|' || COALESCE(min(d)::text,'-') || '..' || COALESCE(max(d)::text,'-') FROM per_hcp" \
  | tee "$EVID/cert_batch_beat_dates.txt"
q "${BEAT_DATES_SQL} SELECT 'territory_dates|' || count(*) || '|' || COALESCE(min(d)::text,'-') || '..' || COALESCE(max(d)::text,'-') FROM territory" \
  | tee -a "$EVID/cert_batch_beat_dates.txt"
q "${BEAT_DATES_SQL} SELECT 'union_dates|' || count(*) || '|' || COALESCE(min(d)::text,'-') || '..' || COALESCE(max(d)::text,'-') FROM all_dates" \
  | tee -a "$EVID/cert_batch_beat_dates.txt"
# Save the dates themselves, not just their span — the coverage check below compares against
# this list, and the Step 1d diff is read against it too.
q "${BEAT_DATES_SQL} SELECT d::text FROM all_dates ORDER BY 1" | tee "$EVID/cert_batch_beat_dates_list.txt"
# Idempotence over a span that COVERS the union, through the SAME previews the ETLs use.
SPAN=$(q "${BEAT_DATES_SQL} SELECT COALESCE(min(d)::text, CURRENT_DATE::text) || ' ' ||
                                   COALESCE((max(d) + 1)::text, CURRENT_DATE::text) FROM all_dates")
# Coverage is asserted, not assumed: every selected date must fall inside [start, end).
q "${BEAT_DATES_SQL}
   SELECT count(*) FROM all_dates
    WHERE d < ('${SPAN%% *}')::date OR d >= ('${SPAN##* }')::date" | tee "$EVID/cert_batch_beat_span_uncovered.txt"
cd "$MAIN" && PYTHONPATH="$MAIN" .venv/bin/dotenv -f .env run -- .venv/bin/python -c "

from src.etl.business_metrics_per_hcp_etl import preview_per_hcp_rollup
from src.etl.territory_metrics_etl import preview_territory_rollup
print(json.dumps({'per_hcp': preview_per_hcp_rollup(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]),
                  'territory': preview_territory_rollup(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])}, default=str))" \
  $SPAN | tee "$EVID/cert_batch_beat_idempotence.json"

That assertion is the only place the r14-02 predicate is proved against a real trigger rather than against a SQL-shape test.
- `pj2_rate_before` = `NULL`. It is what the 03:30 beat must turn into `0.9000`.

**Affected online views, re-derived from the ACTUAL sources and generated values** (codex r14-07). Every view below is reachable by a planted key, and Step 1d's key derivation and reload must cover all of them. Read from `feature_repo/` on 2026-09-15:

| view | source (filter) | entity join keys | reached by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hcp_profile_features` | `hcp_profiles` (no date filter) | `hcp_id` | the 2 planted profiles |
| `goldstd_hcp_cohort_features` | `hcp_profiles` (no date filter) | `hcp_id` | the 2 planted profiles |
| `hcp_conversion_features` | `business_metrics` (365 d, `hcp_id` not null) | `hcp_id`, `hcp_brand_id` | the rows the 03:15 beat writes |
| `hcp_engagement_features` | `business_metrics` (365 d) | `hcp_id`, `hcp_brand_id` | same |
| `trigger_effectiveness_features` | `triggers` (`trigger_date` ≥ 365 d) | `trigger_id`, `hcp_id`, `hcp_brand_id` | the 3 planted triggers |
| `trigger_response_features` | `triggers` (365 d) | `trigger_id` | same |
| `patient_journey_features` | `patient_journeys` (`event_date` ≥ 365 d) | `patient_id`, `patient_brand_id` | the 2 planted journeys — `event_date` = `D1 − 30`, inside the window |
| `patient_adherence_features` | `patient_journeys` (365 d) | `patient_id`, `patient_brand_id` | same |
| **`goldstd_cohort_features`** | `patient_journeys` (`event_date` ≥ **2000 d**) | `patient_id` | same. **This is the view r14-07 says the old text wrongly excluded**; its filter is wider than the others, so no journey inside 365 days can miss it. |
| `territory_performance_features` | `territory_metrics` (365 d) | `territory_id` | the planted territory only. The derivation script must SKIP it and SAY it skipped it — a silent skip here would be indistinguishable from a missed key. |

What the loops will then write, all of it new:
- 03:15 per-HCP: one row per planted (HCP, Kisqali, date) — `market_share = 1.0`, since the planted territory holds only that HCP on that date.
- 03:45 territory: a NEW row for `certproof_trx_canonical_terr` on both dates. Every real territory's row on those dates already exists and is recomputed IDENTICALLY (check 2b proves it; byte-exact because `territory_metrics` has no `updated_at` and no update trigger). No zero rows are written for real territories — that was the pre-Option-A design, where the planted dates were empty.
- 03:30 adherence: selects **both** planted journeys (both arrive in the window) and writes **exactly one** of them. pj_1 has no end date, like every real row, so its rate is preserved and — after codex r14-02 — it is not written at all, timestamp included. pj_2 has a 10-day span and a 9-day duration, so the derivation yields `0.9000` and it is written. `gap_days` is never written for either (Task 22C). `rows_affected = 1` is therefore an exact expectation, not a floor.

**Fallback, only if the planted run is inconclusive:** use the real Monday batch. **First run Step 1d in full and pass its zero-residue proof** (codex r13-04): the fallback does not inherit planted rows, and `cert_batch_planted_marker.txt` records that a plant happened whichever path is finally used. Then restore the reseed cron, under the Step 5 conditions (Task 30 Steps 1–6 complete, `prove_state_post_deploy.txt` exit 0, `post_synthetic_flags.txt` `api == host`), outside the Monday 02:45–04:30 window, and record the restore time as the batch marker. Steps 1b–1c then run after that Monday's 03:15 / 03:45 beats and the next cycle, up to ~7 days later.

```bash
cat "$EVID/post_synthetic_flags.txt"
crontab -l | sed 's|^# HOLD-trx-canonical ||' | crontab -
diff <(crontab -l) "$EVID/crontab_before.txt" && echo "crontab restored"
date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S | tee "$EVID/cert_batch_start_utc.txt"
```

- [ ] **Step 1b: The scheduled loops, not a manual step, populate the online store** (Tasks 22A and 25A, owner decisions #1 and #2)

Run the morning after Step 1a planted the batch (on the fallback path, the morning after the real Monday batch), once all four have happened:
1. The batch has landed: planted at Step 1a, or the host reseed at ~03:01 UTC.
2. The 03:15 per-HCP beat has run.
3. The 03:45 territory beat has run (Step 1c needs it).
4. At least one 6-hourly materializer cycle has STARTED after that rollup (by ~09:30 UTC at the latest).

This step is read-only, and the whole wait is ≤ ~30 h on the default path.

**Nothing here may be run by hand.** If any per-HCP, territory or materialize command is invoked manually between Step 1a and these checks, the proof is void: re-plant (or wait for the next cycle) and start Step 1b again. The point of the step is that the SCHEDULED loops did the work.

**Bind every check to the planted keys** (codex r13-01, owner decision #7). On the planted path the rows the loops created are exactly those with `hcp_id LIKE 'certproof_trx_canonical_%'`, so each query below reads `AND created_at > ${AFTER}` for the time bound and the prefix for identity. The two planted HCPs carry one date each, which is what makes `weekdays >= 2` achievable: one HCP on two dates would collapse to a single newest row under `DISTINCT ON`.

```bash
T_MANUAL=$(cat "$EVID/feast_manual_materialize_utc.txt")    # the LAST manual materialize (Task 30 Step 3b)
T_BATCH=$(cat "$EVID/cert_batch_start_utc.txt")             # planted path: the plant time; fallback: the cron restore
AFTER="GREATEST('${T_MANUAL}+00'::timestamptz, '${T_BATCH}+00'::timestamptz)"
q() { docker exec supabase-db psql -U postgres -d postgres -Atc "$1"; }
# the weekly batch itself
q "SELECT min(created_at), max(created_at), count(*), count(DISTINCT DATE(trigger_timestamp)) FROM triggers WHERE created_at > ${AFTER}" | tee "$EVID/loop_weekly_batch.txt"
# per-HCP rows the SCHEDULED rollup wrote after every manual step, still inside the view's 7-day TTL
q "SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT metric_date), min(created_at), max(created_at) FROM business_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup' AND created_at > ${AFTER} AND event_timestamp >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'" | tee "$EVID/loop_rows_after_manual.txt"
# the loop's own TTL-window runs after the manual step (container log timestamps; also the measured cycle time)
docker logs --timestamps --since "${T_MANUAL}Z" e2i_feast_materializer 2>&1 \
  | grep -E '\[materializer\] (feast materialize [0-9T:-]+ [0-9T:-]+ .*\(bounded lookback\)|cycle complete)' \
  | tee "$EVID/loop_windows_after_manual.txt" | tail -8
# online values for exactly those rows
# codex r14-06: the two paths select DIFFERENTLY and must not share one sed. On the planted
# path identity is the prefix — a time bound alone would let any other post-marker row into
# the first-50 sample and make the weekday count meaningless. On the fallback path there is
# no prefix, so the time bound IS the identity.
if [ -s "$EVID/cert_batch_planted_marker.txt" ] && grep -q '^planted=yes' "$EVID/cert_batch_planted_marker.txt"; then
  SELECT_CLAUSE="WHERE metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup' AND event_timestamp >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days' AND created_at > ${AFTER} AND hcp_id LIKE 'certproof\\_trx\\_canonical\\_%'"
  EXPECT_ENTITIES=2
else
  SELECT_CLAUSE="WHERE metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup' AND event_timestamp >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days' AND created_at > ${AFTER}"
  EXPECT_ENTITIES=""     # fallback: a real batch, count not pinned
fi
sed "s|WHERE event_timestamp >= NOW() - INTERVAL '365 days'|${SELECT_CLAUSE}|" \
  "$EVID/feast_online_check.py" > "$EVID/feast_loop_check.py"
grep -c "created_at > GREATEST('${T_MANUAL}+00'" "$EVID/feast_loop_check.py"
grep -c "certproof" "$EVID/feast_loop_check.py"   # planted path: >= 1; fallback: 0
docker exec -i e2i_feast python - < "$EVID/feast_loop_check.py" | tee "$EVID/feast_loop_check.txt"; echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
# codex r14-06: the sample is keyed, so name the entities it covered and pin them.
q "SELECT hcp_id, metric_date, brand FROM business_metrics
    WHERE metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup' AND created_at > ${AFTER}
      AND hcp_id LIKE 'certproof\\_trx\\_canonical\\_%' ORDER BY hcp_id, metric_date" | tee "$EVID/loop_planted_entities.txt"
```
Expected:
- `loop_weekly_batch.txt`: count > 0 and ≥ 2 distinct trigger dates. **Planted path: exactly `3` triggers on exactly `2` dates** (codex r14-06 — the old "12 rows" was left over from the pre-decision-#7 design that prefixed triggers against six real HCPs; the self-contained plant inserts three). `min(created_at)` = the Step 1a plant time. Fallback: the Monday batch at about 03:00–03:05, normally 7 dates and a count in the hundreds.
- `loop_rows_after_manual.txt`: count > 0, `count(DISTINCT metric_date)` ≥ 2, and `min(created_at)` ≥ that Monday 03:15. A Monday-only result is the pre-fix defect.
- `loop_windows_after_manual.txt`:

  - Record the cycle time: the gap from that cycle's first line to its `cycle complete` line. This is the measurement that replaces Task 25A's unverified 20–30 s projection.
- The first `grep -c` prints `1`. The second prints ≥ 1 on the planted path and `0` on the fallback — if it prints `0` while the marker says `planted=yes`, the sample was NOT bound to the planted identities and the run is void (codex r14-06).
- The loop check prints `checked=<n> mismatches=0 weekdays=<w>` with n > 0, **w ≥ 2**, and `exit=0`.
  - This is the sample on post-fix daily rows: each entity's newest row within the view's 7-day TTL, among this batch's rows, first 50 entities by id.
  - Planted path: **`checked` must be exactly 2 and `w` exactly 2** — no more and no fewer. More than 2 means the prefix filter did not apply and real rows entered the sample; fewer means one planted HCP's row never landed. A `w` of 1 means both planted dates fell on the same weekday (codex r13-01). Every one of these is void, not a warning.
  - `loop_planted_entities.txt` must list exactly two lines, `certproof_trx_canonical_hcp_1 | D1 | Kisqali` and `certproof_trx_canonical_hcp_2 | D2 | Kisqali`, with D1 ≠ D2 and the two dates on different weekdays (codex r14-06: assert the identities, do not infer them from a count).

Together these prove the scheduled rollup and loop populated rows that did not exist at any manual materialize. If the batch has not landed or no cycle has run since, wait. Never count this step as passed with zero rows (the check exits 1 on no rows). Write `LOOP PROVEN` into the report body only when every expectation holds.

- [ ] **Step 1c: The scheduled rollup rolled the whole weekly batch up under each trigger's own date** (Task 22A)

Read-only; same Monday as Step 1b, same shell (`q`, `AFTER`).

**Which dates each assertion is allowed to check** (codex r16-04, same defect as check 2b). The two rollups do NOT select the same dates, so one date set cannot drive both assertions:
- The **per-HCP** beat selects dates by TRIGGER arrival. A trigger-derived CTE is therefore CORRECT for the per-HCP checks — `PER_HCP_DATES` below is deliberately trigger-only, and **must stay that way**. Do not "consistency-fix" it into the union when you see the territory checks use one; it would then assert over dates the per-HCP beat never selected.
- The **territory** beat selects on `bm.created_at` OR a date whose 30-day active-HCP lookback reaches an arrived trigger. A trigger-derived CTE misses the first branch entirely, so a date the territory beat wrote via a recently-created rollup — anything Task 30 Step 3b's backfill produced — was never checked. `TERR_DATES` below is the union.

```bash
PER_HCP_DATES="SELECT DISTINCT DATE(t.trigger_timestamp) AS d FROM triggers t
                WHERE t.created_at > ${AFTER} AND t.hcp_id IS NOT NULL"
TERR_DATES="SELECT DISTINCT bm.metric_date AS d FROM business_metrics bm
             WHERE bm.metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup' AND bm.created_at > ${AFTER}
            UNION
            SELECT DISTINCT bm.metric_date FROM business_metrics bm
             WHERE bm.metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup'
               AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM triggers t
                            WHERE t.created_at > ${AFTER}
                              AND t.trigger_timestamp >= bm.metric_date - INTERVAL '30 days'
                              AND t.trigger_timestamp <  bm.metric_date + INTERVAL '1 day')"
q "WITH batch AS (${PER_HCP_DATES})
   SELECT to_char(b.d, 'Dy YYYY-MM-DD'), count(m.metric_id)
     FROM batch b LEFT JOIN business_metrics m ON m.metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup' AND m.metric_date = b.d
    GROUP BY b.d ORDER BY b.d" | tee "$EVID/rollup_batch_dates.txt"
# Per-HCP shares, over the per-HCP beat's own date set (trigger-derived: correct here).
q "SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT hp.territory_id, m.brand, m.metric_date FROM business_metrics m JOIN hcp_profiles hp ON hp.hcp_id = m.hcp_id WHERE m.metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup' AND m.metric_date IN (${PER_HCP_DATES}) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 HAVING abs(sum(m.market_share) - 1) > 1e-9) x" | tee "$EVID/rollup_batch_share_groups.txt"
# One span covering BOTH selectors, so the two previews below are evaluated over everything
# either beat touched (codex r16-04). Derived from the union, never from triggers alone.
BATCH=$(q "WITH all_d AS (${PER_HCP_DATES} UNION ${TERR_DATES})
           SELECT COALESCE(min(d)::text, CURRENT_DATE::text) || ' ' ||
                  COALESCE((max(d) + 1)::text, CURRENT_DATE::text) FROM all_d")
q "WITH all_d AS (${PER_HCP_DATES} UNION ${TERR_DATES})
   SELECT count(*) FROM all_d WHERE d < ('${BATCH%% *}')::date OR d >= ('${BATCH##* }')::date" \
  | tee "$EVID/rollup_batch_span_uncovered.txt"
cd "$MAIN" && PYTHONPATH="$MAIN" .venv/bin/dotenv -f .env run -- .venv/bin/python -c "
import json, sys
from src.etl.business_metrics_per_hcp_etl import preview_per_hcp_rollup
print(json.dumps(preview_per_hcp_rollup(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]), default=str))" $BATCH | tee "$EVID/rollup_batch_preview.json"
```
Expected:
- `rollup_batch_dates.txt`: EVERY batch date has a count > 0, covering ≥ 2 distinct weekdays. Before the fix, only the Monday line would be non-zero.
- `rollup_batch_share_groups.txt`: `0`.
- `rollup_batch_preview.json`: `rows_new: 0`, `rows_changed: 0` **and `rows_obsolete: 0`** (codex r14-06). The scheduled write equals a whole-date recompute, so no date holds a partial aggregate — and nothing stored on those dates is a row the recompute no longer produces. A non-zero `rows_obsolete` means the scheduled reconcile did not run or did not reach these dates; it is a stop condition, not a note.

Territory (Task 22B, owner decision #3), after the 03:45 beat on the same Monday, same shell:

q "WITH batch AS (${TERR_DATES})

cd "$MAIN" && PYTHONPATH="$MAIN" .venv/bin/dotenv -f .env run -- .venv/bin/python -c "

- `territory_batch_dates.txt`: EVERY batch date has a territory count equal to the territory total (40 on 2026-09-15), and that includes the Tue..Sun dates. Before the fix, only Mondays had rows, and they were written a day late.

Adherence (Task 22C, owner decision #6; execution proof per codex r13-06), after the 03:30 beat on the same morning, same shell.

**Why the proof is a log line PLUS two planted controls.** On live data Task 22C's ETL is a deliberate no-op: 0 of 26,620 journeys have the `journey_end_date` and `journey_duration_days` the derivation needs, so nothing is computable, and after codex r14-02 nothing is written either. A state check over real rows would therefore pass with the 03:30 beat switched off — which is why the committed log line is the primary discriminator (codex r14-05).

But a log line alone proves the task ran, not that its **selection** reached anything. So Step 1a plants a matched pair (owner decision #8 follow-up): pj_1 faithful to production and therefore untouchable, pj_2 computable and therefore written. `rows_affected = 1` — exactly one, from a set of two selected rows — is what proves arrival selection reached the planted journeys AND that the skip predicate held the other one back. Neither half is provable from a `rows_affected = 0` run.

```bash
q "SELECT patient_journey_id,
          COALESCE(round(adherence_rate, 4)::text, 'NULL') AS rate,
          adherent_180d, gap_days, low_gap_180d, updated_at
     FROM patient_journeys
    WHERE patient_journey_id LIKE 'certproof\\_trx\\_canonical\\_%'
    ORDER BY patient_journey_id" | tee "$EVID/adherence_planted_controls.txt"
```
Expected, each a stop condition:
- **pj_2 (positive control)**: `rate = 0.9000`. Still `NULL` means the 03:30 beat did not reach the planted journeys — arrival selection is unproven and certification fails, whatever the log says.
- **pj_1 (negative control)**: `rate = 0.42` **and `updated_at` byte-identical to `pj1_rate_and_updated_at` from Step 1a**. A moved timestamp with an unchanged rate is precisely the r14-02 defect reappearing in production, and the whole-table `patient_journeys` content hash in Step 1d would then also go red — correctly.
- Both rows still satisfy both DGP contracts: pj_1 `0.42 / adherent_180d = 0`, pj_2 `0.9000 / adherent_180d = 1`, both `gap_days = 7 / low_gap_180d = 1`. They are counted by the same invariant query below as every real row; they are not exempt from it.
- The committed log line's `rows_affected` must read **1**.

```bash
WORKER=e2i-causal-analytics-worker_medium-1     # the analytics queue (docker ps, 2026-09-15)
# codex r14-05: grep the COMMITTED line, not the Starting line. Starting is emitted before the
# worker even has a connection, so a run that logs it and then dies in _connect_to_db or in the
# SQL would satisfy a Starting-based check while having done nothing — and every state check
# below would still pass, because Task 22C's ETL is a deliberate no-op on today's data. The
# committed line is emitted only after `with conn:` exits, i.e. after the commit, and carries
# the task id, the selection mode, the window and the row count on one line so it survives
# rotation of the Starting line.
docker logs --timestamps --since "${T_BATCH}Z" "$WORKER" 2>&1 \
  | grep -E "Per-patient adherence rollup committed \[.*\]: selected_by=arrival" \
  | tee "$EVID/adherence_task_ran.txt" | tail -3
grep -c "selected_by=arrival" "$EVID/adherence_task_ran.txt"
# Keep the Starting line too, purely so the pair can be correlated by task id in the report.
docker logs --timestamps --since "${T_BATCH}Z" "$WORKER" 2>&1 \
  | grep -E "Starting per-patient adherence rollup" | tee "$EVID/adherence_task_started.txt" | tail -3
# Negative control 1 — the grep can tell "no run" from "a run": a 90-minute window containing
# no 03:30 slot must yield 0 committed lines.
docker logs --timestamps --since 90m "$WORKER" 2>&1 | grep -c "Per-patient adherence rollup committed" | tee "$EVID/adherence_task_control.txt"
# Negative control 2 — a START WITHOUT A COMMIT must FAIL certification. Run this deliberately,
# once, and keep the output as evidence that the check has teeth. `docker exec -e` sets the
# variable for THIS process only: the container's own environment is not modified, no beat is
# altered, and nothing is written to the database (the connection never opens).
docker exec -e DATABASE_URL='postgresql://nobody@127.0.0.1:1/none' "$WORKER" \
  python -c "from src.etl.patient_adherence_etl import _run_patient_adherence_impl as r; print(r(arrived_before=None)['status'])" \
  2>&1 | tee "$EVID/adherence_negative_control.txt"
grep -c "Starting per-patient adherence rollup" "$EVID/adherence_negative_control.txt"   # must be 1
grep -c "Per-patient adherence rollup committed" "$EVID/adherence_negative_control.txt"  # must be 0
q "SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE adherence_rate = 0), count(*) FILTER (WHERE adherence_rate IS NULL), count(*) FROM patient_journeys" | tee "$EVID/adherence_zero_count.txt"
q "SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE adherent_180d = 1 AND adherence_rate IS NOT NULL AND round(adherence_rate, 4) < 0.80) AS adherence_violations,
          count(*) FILTER (WHERE gap_days IS NOT NULL AND ((gap_days <= 30) <> (low_gap_180d = 1))) AS gap_violations
     FROM patient_journeys" | tee "$EVID/adherence_invariants.txt"
```
Expected:
- `adherence_task_ran.txt`: at least one **committed** line, timestamped after the plant, from that morning's 03:30 slot, carrying `selected_by=arrival`, and `grep -c` prints ≥ 1. **With the 03:30 beat disabled it prints 0 and certification fails** — that is the point of this check. On the planted path its `rows_affected` must read **1** (pj_2 written, pj_1 skipped). On the fallback path, with no planted pair, `rows_affected=0` is the expected healthy value after codex r14-02 and must not be read as "it did not run": there, the presence of the line is the whole proof.
- `adherence_task_started.txt`: the matching `Starting` line. Its task id `[…]` must equal the committed line's, and its window must be the same — that correlation is what makes the pair a single run rather than two unrelated events (codex r14-05).
- `adherence_task_control.txt`: `0`, run at a time of day whose last 90 minutes contain no 03:30 slot. It shows the grep can tell the two cases apart.
- `adherence_negative_control.txt`: `Starting` count `1`, `committed` count **`0`**, and the printed status `failed`. This is the check that distinguishes r14-05's failure mode from a healthy no-op run; if `committed` appears here, the log line is being emitted before the commit and the whole adherence proof is void. Re-run it if the log rotates between the run and the grep.
- `adherence_zero_count.txt`: the `adherence_rate = 0` count equals the baseline (20 before Task 30 Step 3c's repair, 0 after it) and not one row more.
- `adherence_invariants.txt`: `adherence_violations` equals its Step 3c value (6 before the repair, 0 after) and **`gap_violations = 0`**. Both generator contracts were measured intact before the lane (`gap_days <= 30 ⇔ low_gap_180d = 1`: 7,980 / 18,620, zero violations), and Task 22C must not create a single new violation (codex r13-05).

Write `ROLLUP PROVEN` into the report body only when every expectation holds: per-HCP, territory and adherence.

- [ ] **Step 1d: Remove the planted batch and prove it is gone** (owner decisions #5 and #7)

Mandatory whenever `cert_batch_planted_marker.txt` exists, whichever proof path is chosen. If the planted run is inconclusive, this step runs BEFORE switching to the real-Monday fallback (codex r13-04): the fallback does not inherit planted rows. It runs after Steps 1b and 1c pass and BEFORE Step 2 captures the tuple, so the certified state contains no planted row. The materialize here comes AFTER the loop proof, so it cannot flatter it.

**(1) Stop the materializer first, and keep it stopped for the whole of parts (2)–(3)** (codex r14-01). The 6-hourly loop is the one process that can re-create a planted online key between the delete and the proof, and it does so silently: a cycle that starts while the planted rows are still in Postgres writes them straight back. Stopping it also keeps the online state still between part (2)'s key deletes and part (5)'s absence proof.

```bash
q() { docker exec supabase-db psql -U postgres -d postgres -Atc "$1"; }
docker inspect e2i_feast_materializer --format '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.StartedAt}}' | tee "$EVID/materializer_before_cleanup.txt"
docker stop e2i_feast_materializer
docker inspect e2i_feast_materializer --format '{{.State.Status}}' | tee -a "$EVID/materializer_before_cleanup.txt"
```
Expected: the second line reads `exited`. It is restarted and re-proved in part (4); if any of parts (2)–(3) aborts, restart it by hand before reporting — a permanently stopped materializer is its own outage.

**(2) Delete the planted ONLINE keys, derived from the actual source rows** (codex r13-02, r14-01). Redis keeps the newer event time, so a reload cannot undo a planted newest value. `_redis_key` is `serialize_entity_key(entity_key, version) + project` (`feast/infra/online_stores/helpers.py`), the project is `e2i_causal_analytics` and `entity_key_serialization_version` is 3 (`/feast/feature_store.yaml`).

**This part runs BEFORE part (3)'s row deletes, not after** — the derivation reads the planted rows through each view's own source query, so the rows must still exist. Order for the whole step: (1) stop the materializer → (2) derive keys and delete them → (3) delete the Postgres rows → (4) reload → (5) prove.

**Why it is derived and not written down.** The earlier version listed the keys as literals, including `hcp_brand_id = f"{hcp}_Kisqali"` while the plant inserted `brand_id = 'UNKNOWN'`. `triggers.hcp_brand_id` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (hcp_id || '_' || COALESCE(brand_id,'UNKNOWN'))`, so the real key was `…_UNKNOWN`: the delete would have removed a key that never existed, `residual` would have been 0, and the planted features would have stayed online behind a green check. Fixing the literal would fix that one case and leave the method — assume the key — intact. Six of these columns are generated on `triggers` and four on `patient_journeys`; the only reliable source of a key's value is the row itself.

```bash
cat > "$EVID/delete_planted_online_keys.py" <<'PY'
"""Derive every planted online key FROM ITS VIEW'S OWN SOURCE ROWS, delete it, prove it is gone.

For each registered FeatureView: take its entity join keys from the registry, run its own
batch-source query as a subquery, and select the DISTINCT join-key tuples whose values carry
the certproof prefix. Those tuples ARE the entity keys Feast materialized — generated columns,
COALESCE branches, source filters and all. Nothing here is assumed.
"""
import json
import psycopg
import redis
from feast import FeatureStore
from feast.infra.online_stores.helpers import _redis_key
from feast.protos.feast.types.EntityKey_pb2 import EntityKey as EntityKeyProto
from feast.protos.feast.types.Value_pb2 import Value as ValueProto

PREFIX = "certproof_trx_canonical_"
store = FeatureStore(repo_path="/feast")
off = store.config.offline_store
dsn = (f"host={off.host} port={off.port} dbname={off.database} user={off.user} "
       f"password={getattr(off, 'password', None)} sslmode={getattr(off, 'sslmode', 'prefer')}")
host, port = store.config.online_store.connection_string.split(",")[0].split(":")
password = next((p.split("=", 1)[1] for p in store.config.online_store.connection_string.split(",")
                 if p.startswith("password=")), None)
client = redis.Redis(host=host, port=int(port), password=password)
version = store.config.entity_key_serialization_version

derived, skipped, report = [], [], []
with psycopg.connect(dsn) as conn:
    for fv in sorted(store.list_feature_views(), key=lambda v: v.name):
        join_keys = []
        for ent in fv.entities:
            join_keys += store.get_entity(ent).join_keys
        join_keys = list(dict.fromkeys(join_keys))
        query = getattr(fv.batch_source, "query", None)
        if not query:
            skipped.append((fv.name, "source has no SQL query"))
            continue
        cols = ", ".join(f"s.{k}" for k in join_keys)
        pred = " OR ".join(f"s.{k}::text LIKE %s" for k in join_keys)
        sql = f"SELECT DISTINCT {cols} FROM ({query}) s WHERE {pred}"
        try:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(sql, [f"{PREFIX}%"] * len(join_keys))
                rows = cur.fetchall()
        except psycopg.Error as e:
            conn.rollback()
            # A join key the source does not select (market_dynamics_features: territory_id and
            # brand_id are absent from business_metrics_source) cannot have been materialized
            # from it. Record it LOUDLY — a silent skip is indistinguishable from a missed key.
            skipped.append((fv.name, str(e).splitlines()[0]))
            continue
        for row in rows:
            derived.append({"view": fv.name, "keys": dict(zip(join_keys, [str(v) for v in row]))})
        report.append((fv.name, join_keys, len(rows)))

seen, deleted, residual = set(), 0, 0
for item in derived:
    keys = item["keys"]
    sig = tuple(sorted(keys.items()))
    if sig in seen:
        continue
    seen.add(sig)
    ek = EntityKeyProto(join_keys=list(keys),
                        entity_values=[ValueProto(string_val=v) for v in keys.values()])
    rk = _redis_key(store.project, ek, entity_key_serialization_version=version)
    deleted += client.delete(rk)
    residual += client.exists(rk)

json.dump({"derived": derived, "skipped": skipped, "per_view": report},
          open("/feast/data/planted_online_keys.json", "w"), indent=1)
for name, jk, n in report:
    print(f"  {name}: join_keys={jk} planted_rows={n}")
for name, why in skipped:
    print(f"  SKIPPED {name}: {why}")
print(f"views={len(report)} skipped={len(skipped)} distinct_keys={len(seen)} "
      f"deleted={deleted} residual={residual}")
raise SystemExit(0 if residual == 0 else 1)
PY
docker exec -i e2i_feast python - < "$EVID/delete_planted_online_keys.py" | tee "$EVID/cert_batch_online_keys.txt"; echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
docker cp e2i_feast:/feast/data/planted_online_keys.json "$EVID/planted_online_keys.json"
```
Expected, each a stop condition:
- `residual=0` and exit 0.
- The per-view lines must include a non-zero `planted_rows` for **every** view in Step 1a's affected-view table: `hcp_profile_features`, `goldstd_hcp_cohort_features`, `hcp_conversion_features`, `hcp_engagement_features`, `trigger_effectiveness_features`, `trigger_response_features`, `patient_journey_features`, `patient_adherence_features`, **`goldstd_cohort_features`** and `territory_performance_features`. A zero where the table says a view is reachable is a finding: either the plant did not reach it or the derivation is wrong — do not proceed on the assumption that "nothing to delete" means "nothing is there".
- The only acceptable `SKIPPED` line is `market_dynamics_features` (its join keys `territory_id` / `brand_id` are not selected by `business_metrics_source`, so it cannot materialize from it). Any other skip is a stop condition.
- Cross-check the derived values against the plant readout: `planted_online_keys.json` must contain `hcp_brand_id` values ending in `_Kisqali` and none ending in `_UNKNOWN` (codex r14-01).
- `deleted` may be lower than `distinct_keys` when a view's key was never materialized; `residual` is the gate, and the per-view expectations above are what stop that from hiding a miss.

**(3) Exact deletes, FK-safe order, no whole-table restore** (owner decisions #7 and #9). EVERY row is addressed by prefix — there is no date-scoped arm any more. Under Option A the planted dates carry real rows that the beats recomputed identically, so a date scope would delete data this cert must leave untouched.

```bash
read -r _ D1 D2 <<<"$(tr '=' ' ' < "$EVID/cert_batch_planted_marker.txt" | awk '{print $2, $4, $6}')"
docker exec -i supabase-db psql -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v d1="$D1" -v d2="$D2" <<'SQL' | tee "$EVID/cert_batch_cleanup.txt"
BEGIN;
-- codex r15-02 + r15-03: BEFORE the first delete, lock the planted parents and assert that
-- NOTHING anywhere references them. The old gate ran after four deletes and covered children of
-- `hcp_profiles` only, so a CASCADE child of `triggers` or `patient_journeys` (there are four)
-- was already gone by the time it looked — invisible to it, to the content hashes and to the
-- prefix residue checks alike. This gate is GENERATED from pg_constraint so a new FK is covered
-- the day it lands, rather than the day someone remembers to edit a list.
DO $$
DECLARE
    r        record;
    n        bigint;
    bad      text := '';
    covered  text[];
    cascaded text[];
    gap      text[];
BEGIN
    -- (a) Lock the planted parent rows. An FK insert takes FOR KEY SHARE on its parent row, and
    -- FOR UPDATE conflicts with that, so from here no concurrent writer can add a child row that
    -- would slip between this check and the deletes below (codex r15-03).
    PERFORM 1 FROM public.hcp_profiles    WHERE hcp_id             LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%' FOR UPDATE;
    PERFORM 1 FROM public.triggers        WHERE trigger_id         LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%' FOR UPDATE;
    PERFORM 1 FROM public.patient_journeys WHERE patient_journey_id LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%' FOR UPDATE;

    -- (b) No FK may point at a parent whose key does NOT carry the prefix, or the count below
    -- would be vacuously zero. business_metrics.metric_id is an md5 and territory_metrics has a
    -- composite key; neither has an incoming FK today, and if one appears this must be revisited.
    SELECT array_agg(DISTINCT c.confrelid::regclass::text) INTO gap
      FROM pg_constraint c
     WHERE c.contype = 'f'
       AND c.confrelid::regclass::text IN ('business_metrics', 'territory_metrics');
    IF gap IS NOT NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'a FK now references % — its key carries no certproof prefix, so the '
                        'child check below would be vacuous. Revisit before deleting.', gap;
    END IF;

    -- (c) Every child of every deleted parent, by prefix, generated from the catalog.
    FOR r IN
        SELECT c.conrelid::regclass::text AS child,
               a.attname::text            AS col,
               c.confrelid::regclass::text AS parent
          FROM pg_constraint c
          JOIN unnest(c.conkey) WITH ORDINALITY k(attnum, ord) ON true
          JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = c.conrelid AND a.attnum = k.attnum
         WHERE c.contype = 'f'
           AND c.confrelid::regclass::text IN ('triggers', 'patient_journeys', 'hcp_profiles')
           AND c.conrelid::regclass::text NOT IN
               ('triggers', 'business_metrics', 'territory_metrics', 'patient_journeys', 'hcp_profiles')
    LOOP
        EXECUTE format('SELECT count(*) FROM public.%I WHERE %I::text LIKE %L',
                       r.child, r.col, 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%') INTO n;
        covered := array_append(covered, r.child);
        IF n <> 0 THEN
            bad := bad || format('%s.%s -> %s = %s row(s); ', r.child, r.col, r.parent, n);
        END IF;
    END LOOP;

    -- (d) One generated level is enough ONLY IF every table a delete can CASCADE into was
    -- checked above: if none of them holds a referencing row, nothing below them can be
    -- affected either, by induction. Prove that premise rather than assuming it.
    SELECT array_agg(DISTINCT c.conrelid::regclass::text) INTO cascaded
      FROM pg_constraint c
     WHERE c.contype = 'f' AND c.confdeltype = 'c'
       AND c.confrelid::regclass::text IN ('triggers', 'patient_journeys', 'hcp_profiles');
    SELECT array_agg(t) INTO gap
      FROM unnest(COALESCE(cascaded, '{}')) t
     WHERE NOT t = ANY (COALESCE(covered, '{}'));
    IF gap IS NOT NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'CASCADE target(s) % were not covered by the child check — a deeper '
                        'layer could be deleted or nulled unseen', gap;
    END IF;

    IF bad <> '' THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'certproof rows are referenced, so a delete would CASCADE or SET NULL '
                        'them silently: %. Report, do not force.', bad;
    END IF;
END $$;
DELETE FROM public.triggers        WHERE trigger_id LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%';
DELETE FROM public.business_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup' AND hcp_id LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%';
-- OWNER DECISION #9 (Option A): PREFIX-ONLY. The old `OR metric_date IN (d1, d2)` arm was
-- correct only while the planted dates were proven EMPTY; under Option A the planted date
-- carries REAL territory rows that the 03:45 beat recomputed identically, and a date-scoped
-- delete would destroy them. The r14-04 ownership predicate is kept: a row an independent
-- writer has touched is never deleted even under the prefix.
--
-- Nothing becomes unreachable by dropping the date arm, and this is structural rather than
-- lucky: `territory_metrics_etl.py:191-195` builds its territory list as
-- `SELECT DISTINCT territory_id FROM hcp_profiles`, so the ONLY territory row the plant can
-- create is its own `certproof_trx_canonical_terr` — every other territory already existed and
-- already had a row on that date. The prefix arm therefore covers the whole planted set.
DELETE FROM public.territory_metrics
 WHERE territory_id LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%'
   AND market_potential IS NULL AND resource_allocation_score IS NULL;
DELETE FROM public.patient_journeys WHERE patient_journey_id LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%';
-- The child-emptiness gate already ran, generated, BEFORE the first delete (top of this
-- transaction, codex r15-02). What remains here is specific to the profile delete's own
-- on-delete side effect, measured 2026-09-15: triggers.hcp_id -> hcp_profiles is NO ACTION so a
-- missed trigger BLOCKS and is caught, but business_metrics.hcp_id -> hcp_profiles is
-- **ON DELETE SET NULL** — a missed per-HCP row would NOT block. Postgres would null its hcp_id,
-- and since hcp_id is the row's ONLY certproof marker (metric_id is an md5), the residue check
-- would then read 0: a false green hiding an orphaned rollup row with planted values.
DO $$
DECLARE strays int; nulls_before int; nulls_after int;
BEGIN
    SELECT count(*) INTO strays FROM public.business_metrics
     WHERE hcp_id LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%';
    IF strays <> 0 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'business_metrics still holds % certproof row(s); deleting the profiles '
                        'would SET NULL their hcp_id and hide them from the residue check', strays;
    END IF;
    -- codex r15-03: scoped to per_hcp_rollup, not the whole table. A table-wide NULL count
    -- races the seasonality writers, which legitimately insert NULL-hcp_id market-scale
    -- rows (measured 2026-09-15: 9,900 of them, all metric_type trx/nrx/market_share/
    -- conversion_rate/hcp_engagement_score, and ZERO per_hcp_rollup). A laundered row
    -- would be per_hcp_rollup by construction, so this scope is both exact and immune to
    -- the benign writers. The FOR UPDATE above is the primary guarantee; this is the
    -- check that catches a row the prefix scan somehow missed.
    SELECT count(*) INTO nulls_before FROM public.business_metrics
     WHERE hcp_id IS NULL AND metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup';
    -- The profile delete lives INSIDE this block so the ON DELETE SET NULL side effect can be
    -- measured across it. A row nulled here would be a certproof rollup row that escaped the
    -- prefix delete, and after nulling no prefix query can ever find it again.
    DELETE FROM public.hcp_profiles WHERE hcp_id LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%';

    SELECT count(*) INTO nulls_after FROM public.business_metrics
     WHERE hcp_id IS NULL AND metric_type = 'per_hcp_rollup';
    IF nulls_after <> nulls_before THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'deleting the planted profiles nulled % per_hcp_rollup hcp_id(s) '
                        '(% -> %, baseline is 0): an orphaned rollup row escaped the prefix delete',
                        nulls_after - nulls_before, nulls_before, nulls_after;
    END IF;
END $$;
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM public.triggers WHERE trigger_id LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%') AS trig,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM public.business_metrics WHERE hcp_id LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%') AS per_hcp,
       -- codex r18-01: planted IDENTITIES only. The old `OR metric_date IN (d1, d2)` arm is the
       -- mirror of the one removed from the DELETE above, and it survived the migration: under
       -- Option A the real territory rows on D1/D2 are PRESERVED by design, so that arm counts
       -- them, reports terr > 0, and fails a cleanup that in fact succeeded. What we mean is
       -- "our rows are gone" — this count — AND "their rows are untouched", which the full-row
       -- D1/D2 hash buckets in part (5) prove. One zero-count never said both.
       (SELECT count(*) FROM public.territory_metrics
         WHERE territory_id LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%') AS terr,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM public.patient_journeys WHERE patient_journey_id LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%') AS journeys,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM public.hcp_profiles WHERE hcp_id LIKE 'certproof\_trx\_canonical\_%') AS hcps;
COMMIT;
SQL
```
All five counts must be 0 inside the transaction — and all five now count **planted identities**, not dates (codex r18-01). `terr = 0` means every planted territory row is gone; it says nothing about the real rows on D1/D2, which are *supposed* to survive and whose preservation is proved separately by the unchanged D1/D2 full-row hash buckets in part (5). Those two assertions together are the actual requirement: our rows gone, their rows untouched. The per-HCP delete keys on `hcp_id`, because the rollup's `metric_id` is an md5 and carries no prefix — which is exactly why the `ON DELETE SET NULL` gate above matters: `hcp_id` is the ONLY certproof marker a per-HCP row carries, and the profile delete is able to erase it. Either exception aborts the whole transaction; report it and do not force the delete.

**(4) Bring the materializer back up.** Nothing to restore (owner decision #9). The claim this step makes, and the only one it makes, is that **no real territory's online entry serves a value that differs from its own newest offline source row.** Entries may APPEAR where none existed — the materializer writing a correct value for a previously-absent key, which the Redis skip cannot prevent because `prev_event_time` is falsy there — and that is NOT a failure: the source is unchanged, the value is right, and the scheduled materializer would have written it at its next run anyway, so the cert at most advances the timing. Absence is pre-existing, reported and not failed. What the plant DID create is gone — its source rows by part (3), its online keys by part (2) — and part (5) proves both.

**What used to be here, and which review findings went with it.** This slot held a territory-wide online restore: delete every territory key, reload the view, and prove the result. Three findings shaped it, and all three are moot for the same reason — under Option A the plant leaves every real territory's offline source rows unchanged (check 2b, zero new and zero changed over the prospective union), so the materializer's input for those territories is exactly what it would have been without the plant, and there is no altered value for a restore to put back:
- **r14-08** required the restoration to be proved rather than asserted — a pre-plant snapshot plus a three-way after-comparison. Nothing is restored now, so there is nothing to prove.
- **r15-05** required "reconstructible" to mean the reload REPRODUCES the saved state, values and absence included, not merely that a recent source row exists. No key is deleted, so no reload has to reproduce anything.
- **r16-03** corrected that gate to compare against the saved pre-plant state rather than the current (planted) one. The gate is gone.

**The premise — corrected after codex r19-01, which found the original argument resting on an unproven precondition.** The note used to say: the planted dates are `<=` the newest real territory row, so Redis skips the planted write and no real online entry moves. The `<=` comparison is real (`feast/infra/online_stores/redis.py:313`, feast **0.43.0**, verified, and version parity confirmed for `.venv` and the running `e2i_feast` container). But look at what encloses it:

```python
# ignore if event_timestamp is before the event features that are currently in the feature store
if prev_event_time:                                   # <-- the precondition we never established
    prev_ts = Timestamp()
    prev_ts.ParseFromString(prev_event_time)
    if prev_ts.seconds and event_time_seconds <= prev_ts.seconds:
        ...
        continue
```
The skip happens **only for a key that already has a stored timestamp**. For a territory whose online entry is absent or carries no `_ts`, `prev_event_time` is falsy, the guard never engages, and the write lands. A global `max(metric_date)` read from Postgres cannot establish that precondition per key, and neither the content hashes nor the planted-key absence check say anything about it. **We do not know whether real territory keys are present**, and this plan does not claim to: an attempt to measure it produced a probe whose own positive control returned all-None, which cannot distinguish "the store is empty" from "the probe cannot read it". (Context, not evidence: this lane folds in a known defect where `materialize-incremental` left the online store all-None, so the question is live rather than theoretical.)

**The preservation argument therefore does not use the guard at all.** It rests on source invariance, which IS established, by a stop condition already in this plan:
1. Check 2b requires `rows_new = 0` and `rows_changed = 0` over the **prospective** union, which since codex r17-02 includes D1/D2 and the territory dates the planted arrivals reach. So the beats create no new `(territory, metric_date)` cell for any real territory and alter no existing one.
2. Byte-exactly so: `territory_metrics` has no `updated_at` and no update trigger, and the `ON CONFLICT` SET arm never touches `created_at`.
3. Therefore every real territory's offline source rows are identical before and after the plant — so whatever the materializer writes for a real territory, with the guard engaged or not, is **the value it would have written had the plant never happened**. Presence or absence of a prior key cannot change that, because the input to the write is unchanged.

The `<=` skip is now a secondary remark, true where a stored timestamp exists and relied upon nowhere. **If a future change makes the recompute non-idempotent, this argument fails and the deleted restore machinery becomes necessary again** — which is why check 2b's zero-change requirement is a STOP CONDITION and not a warning.

**This does not reopen owner decision #9.** Option A's grounds are independent: the old empty-date predicate is structurally unsatisfiable (1,142 of 1,143 days carry triggers), the prefix-only delete is complete by construction (`territory_metrics_etl.py:191-195` draws territories from `hcp_profiles`, so the plant can only create its own), and disjointness plus idempotence covers the Postgres side. What r19-01 corrected is one supporting argument inside this note, not the decision.

**Retired with its operation — NOT proved safe.** These questions are unasked because the operation that raised them no longer happens, which is a different kind of closure from having shown the operation harmless. The distinction matters whenever machinery is deleted rather than fixed: **a deletion note that does not say which of the two it is will be read as "we proved it safe", and that is precisely what was not done.** Trigger condition: **if any future change reintroduces a territory-wide online key delete, r15-05 and r16-03 return with it and the deleted gate must be rebuilt** — do not treat this note as having settled them.

```bash
docker start e2i_feast_materializer
docker inspect e2i_feast_materializer --format '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.StartedAt}}' | tee "$EVID/materializer_after_cleanup.txt"
sleep 20; docker logs --tail 5 --timestamps e2i_feast_materializer 2>&1 | tee -a "$EVID/materializer_after_cleanup.txt"
```
Expected: status `running`, a `StartedAt` later than `materializer_before_cleanup.txt`'s, and recent log lines. The step stopped a scheduled loop; leaving it stopped would be an outage introduced by the certification.

**(5) Zero-residue and unchanged-content proof.**

**The concurrency boundary, stated before the proof is read** (codex r14-03). An identity hash is only meaningful once you can say who else was allowed to write. During the ~30 h window:
- The **reseed cron is HELD** (Step 5 restores it), so nothing writes `triggers`, `hcp_profiles` or `patient_journeys` except the plant and this cleanup. Their hashes must be identical, full stop.
- Three Celery beats run and are *supposed* to write: 03:15 per-HCP, 03:30 adherence, 03:45 territory. **They do NOT touch only D1 and D2** — an earlier draft claimed that and it is false (codex r15-04). The arrival window is 174 h, so every REAL trigger that arrived in the last weekly batch is still eligible for up to seven days after it landed, and the territory variant additionally selects any date within the 30-day active-HCP reach of an arrived trigger. Holding the cron stops NEW arrivals; it does not retire the ones already inside the window. So the scheduled runs will legitimately recompute a set of real dates as well, and the baseline hash can only be an identity if those recomputations are **content-preserving**. That is provable, not assumable, and Step 1a's preflight proves it — see *The dates the beats will touch* below.
  - Why an idempotent recompute leaves the bytes identical, measured 2026-09-15: `business_metrics` and `territory_metrics` have **no `updated_at` column and no update trigger** (unlike `hcp_profiles`, `triggers` and `patient_journeys`, which all carry `update_*_timestamp`), and the `ON CONFLICT` SET arms never touch `created_at`. So an upsert that writes the same aggregates produces the same `x::text`. If either table ever gains an `updated_at`, this proof goes red — correctly, because the claim would no longer hold.
- The 03:30 adherence beat writes `patient_journeys` — and after codex r14-02 it writes nothing where no value would change, which is **every non-certproof row**: 0 of 26,620 have the `journey_end_date` and `journey_duration_days` the derivation needs. It does write exactly one row, the planted positive control **pj_2**, and that row is excluded from the hash by the `x::text NOT LIKE '%certproof_trx_canonical_%'` predicate like every other planted row. So `patient_journeys` can be hashed as an identity rather than excluded — and if r14-02's predicate were ever removed, the ~153 real rows the run selects would all get a fresh `updated_at` and this proof would go red, correctly.
  - Note the asymmetry deliberately: the *count* the beat reports (`rows_affected = 1`) and the *set the hash covers* are disjoint by construction. Step 1c asserts the former on the planted pair; this hash asserts the latter on everything else. Neither can mask a failure of the other.
- Anything else that writes these five tables during the window is outside the design and the hash is supposed to catch it. A mismatch is a finding to report, never a threshold to widen.

```bash
# Redefined verbatim here: Step 1a ran a day earlier, in another shell. It must be the SAME
# text as the preflight's, or the diff compares two different questions.
cksum() {   # $1 = table. One line, whole-row hash of every non-certproof row.
  # No GROUP BY: Postgres rejects `GROUP BY NULL` with "non-integer constant in GROUP BY"
  # (verified 2026-09-15). The two rollup tables get their own date-bucketed queries below.
  q "SELECT '$1|all|' || count(*) || '|' || md5(string_agg(x::text, ',' ORDER BY x::text))
       FROM (SELECT * FROM public.$1) x
      WHERE x::text NOT LIKE '%certproof_trx_canonical_%'"
}
{ cksum triggers; cksum hcp_profiles; cksum patient_journeys
  q "SELECT 'business_metrics|' || x.metric_date || '|' || count(*) || '|' || md5(string_agg(x::text, ',' ORDER BY x::text))

"""No planted entity key is served by ANY affected view after the cleanup.

Reads the keys part (2) derived from the real source rows, and asks the online store for each
one through every view that key belongs to. Absence means every requested feature is None.
"""
import json, sys
from feast import FeatureStore

store = FeatureStore(repo_path="/feast")
derived = json.load(open("/feast/data/planted_online_keys.json"))["derived"]
by_view = {}
for item in derived:
    by_view.setdefault(item["view"], []).append(item["keys"])

served, checked = [], 0
for view_name, rows in sorted(by_view.items()):
    fv = store.get_feature_view(view_name)
    join_keys = set(rows[0])
    names = [f.name for f in fv.schema if f.name not in join_keys]
    if not names:
        continue
    refs = [f"{view_name}:{n}" for n in names]
    resp = store.get_online_features(features=refs, entity_rows=rows).to_dict()
    for i, keys in enumerate(rows):
        checked += 1
        vals = {n: resp[n][i] for n in names if n in resp}
        if any(v is not None for v in vals.values()):
            served.append({"view": view_name, "keys": keys, "still_served": vals})
print(f"views={len(by_view)} keys_checked={checked} still_served={len(served)}")
for s in served[:10]:
    print("  STILL SERVED:", s)
sys.exit(0 if not served else 1)

This is the after-verification for the preservation argument — which rests on source invariance, not on Redis's skip guard, so what it checks is that the values actually served match the unchanged source. **Absence is not a failure here**: whether real territory keys are populated at all is a pre-existing question this lane does not resolve (see the premise note in part (4)), and an absent entry is neither caused by nor evidence against the cleanup. A territory that HAS an entry and serves something other than its newest source row IS a failure, and the one this check exists to catch.

```bash
cat > "$EVID/territory_parity_check.py" <<'PY3'
"""Served territory values match the newest offline source row, for entries that exist."""
import json, math, sys

import numpy as np
import psycopg
from feast import FeatureStore
from feast.types import Float32, Int32, Int64


def _mismatch(want, served, dtype) -> bool:
    """True when `served` differs from `want` for a field declared as `dtype` (codex r20-01).

    Shaped by the FIELD TYPE, not by one tolerance:
      * non-finite FIRST — `abs(x - nan)` is `nan` and `nan > tol` is False, so any
        tolerance comparison silently reads a served NaN against a finite source as EQUAL;
      * Int64 — compare exactly; a bigint difference is never sub-unit;
      * Float32 — the view declares Float32 while the source column is `double precision`,
        so round BOTH sides through float32 before comparing. A raw 1e-9 tolerance calls a
        correct round-trip a mismatch (0.1 -> 0.10000000149011612, diff 1.49e-09).
    """
    if (want is None) != (served is None):
        return True
    if want is None:
        return False
    w_bad = isinstance(want, float) and not math.isfinite(want)
    s_bad = isinstance(served, float) and not math.isfinite(served)
    if w_bad or s_bad:
        if w_bad and s_bad:
            if math.isnan(want) and math.isnan(served):
                return False
            return want != served
        return True
    if dtype in (Int64, Int32):
        return int(want) != int(served)
    if dtype == Float32:
        return np.float32(want) != np.float32(served)
    return abs(float(want) - float(served)) > 1e-9


def main() -> int:
    """Executable body, guarded so the controls below can import `_mismatch` without
    opening a DB connection or running the parity sweep (codex r20-01)."""
    store = FeatureStore(repo_path="/feast")
    off = store.config.offline_store
    dsn = (f"host={off.host} port={off.port} dbname={off.database} user={off.user} "
           f"password={getattr(off, 'password', None)} sslmode={getattr(off, 'sslmode', 'prefer')}")
    fv = store.get_feature_view("territory_performance_features")
    names = [f.name for f in fv.schema if f.name != "territory_id"]
    dtypes = {f.name: f.dtype for f in fv.schema}   # declared types drive the comparison
    refs = [f"{fv.name}:{n}" for n in names]

    with psycopg.connect(dsn) as conn, conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(f"""
            SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.territory_id) s.territory_id, to_jsonb(s)
              FROM ({store.get_data_source("territory_metrics_source").query}) s
             ORDER BY s.territory_id, s.event_timestamp DESC, s.created_at DESC
        """)
        newest = dict(cur.fetchall())

    rows = [{"territory_id": t} for t in sorted(newest)]
    resp = store.get_online_features(features=refs, entity_rows=rows).to_dict()
    missing_cols = [n for n in names if n not in resp]
    if missing_cols:
        print(f"RESPONSE SHAPE UNEXPECTED: {missing_cols}; keys={sorted(resp)[:8]}")
        sys.exit(1)

    absent, mismatched = [], []
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        tid = r["territory_id"]
        served = {n: resp[n][i] for n in names}
        if all(v is None for v in served.values()):
            absent.append(tid)
            continue
        want = {n: newest[tid].get(n) for n in names}
        diff = {n: (want[n], served[n]) for n in names if _mismatch(want[n], served[n], dtypes[n])}
        if diff:
            mismatched.append({"territory_id": tid, "diff": diff})
    json.dump({"absent": absent, "mismatched": mismatched},
              open("/feast/data/territory_parity.json", "w"), indent=1, default=str)
    print(f"territories={len(rows)} served={len(rows)-len(absent)} absent={len(absent)} "
          f"mismatched={len(mismatched)}")
    for m in mismatched[:10]:
        print("  MISMATCH:", m)
    return 0 if not mismatched else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
PY3

```bash

import sys
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0, "/feast/data")
from territory_parity_check import _mismatch   # import-safe: its body is under __main__
from feast.types import Float32, Int64

CONTROLS = [
    ("1. Float32 0.1 served as its float32 round-trip", 0.1, float(np.float32(0.1)), Float32, False),
    ("2. finite source served as NaN",                  1234.0, float("nan"),        Float32, True),
    ("3. Int64 off by one",                             1234,   1235,                Int64,   True),
    ("4. identical pair",                               1234,   1234,                Int64,   False),
]
bad = 0
for label, want, served, dtype, expected in CONTROLS:
    got = bool(_mismatch(want, served, dtype))
    ok = got == expected
    bad += not ok
    print(f"{label:50} mismatch={str(got):5} expected={str(expected):5} {'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
print(f"controls_failed={bad}")
sys.exit(0 if bad == 0 else 1)

Expected — **measured 2026-09-15 against this exact comparator**, then written down (not the other way round):
```
1. Float32 0.1 served as its float32 round-trip    mismatch=False expected=False OK
2. finite source served as NaN                     mismatch=True  expected=True  OK
3. Int64 off by one                                mismatch=True  expected=True  OK
4. identical pair                                  mismatch=False expected=False OK

Also measured on the same run, as the teeth: the OLD comparator scores control 2 as `abs(1234.0 - nan) > 1e-9` → **False**, i.e. it reports a served NaN as a MATCH — that is the false green this replaces. `NaN vs NaN` → `False` (identical non-finite is a match), `0.4567` round-trip → `False` (no spurious mismatch), and a genuinely wrong Float32 `0.1 vs 0.2` → `True` (real errors still caught). `controls_failed` must be `0`; a non-zero value means the comparator cannot see the failure the parity check exists to find, and the parity result that follows it means nothing.

**Latent, not live — do not read this as a repaired cert risk.** Neither failure mode can fire on today's data, measured read-only over the source query's own 365-day window: `territory_metrics` holds 1,840 rows with `total_trx`, `active_hcp_count` and `covered_lives` **1840/1840 populated** (the positive control — the probe can see values), while `market_potential` and `resource_allocation_score` are **0/1840 populated in the window and 0/1840 over the whole table ever**. So every value reaching the arithmetic today is a `bigint`, where `float()` is exact and any real difference is ≥ 1; the two `Float32` fields are NULL on both sides and take the `(want is None) != (served is None)` branch, never the numeric one. This hardens the check against **a real Reltio/Veeva integration landing** — a documented planned block, not a vague someday. Primary evidence, `src/etl/territory_metrics_etl.py:24-40`, under its own heading *"Why `market_potential` and `resource_allocation_score` stay NULL"*: *"The plan calls for both columns to be populated from real Reltio/Veeva sources when available, NULL otherwise. Migration 031's seed values were `random()` placeholders — the scaffolding this ETL replaces."* It lists the two steps a future block takes (add a Reltio/Veeva mirror table; re-enable the SET clauses), writes `CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE PRECISION)` explicitly on insert (`:295-296`), and has `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` omit both columns so any surviving 031 seed is not overwritten. `src/workers/celery_app.py:388` says it in one line: *"market_potential / resource_allocation_score remain NULL until a real Reltio/Veeva source lands."* Secondary, and about the CONSUMER's honest handling of the NULLs rather than the intent behind them: `resource_optimizer.py:810-816` records both as "100% NULL" with no other budget source.

**And this is the strongest argument for typing the comparator rather than loosening its tolerance.** Those columns are NULL by deliberate ANTI-FABRICATION design: 031's `random()` placeholders were removed precisely so nobody could read a plausible-wrong number as real. A comparator that silently accepts a NaN against a finite source would reintroduce exactly that failure one layer out, at serving time — a fabricated value passing a green check. That is why this is worth hardening even though neither failure mode can fire on today's data, and it is not a repair of a live defect. Overstating it would be the same error as the claims retracted earlier in this lane.
- `cert_batch_cleanup_online_absence.txt`: `still_served=0`, exit 0, and `views=` equal to the number of views part (2) derived keys for. This is the check that covers the other nine; a non-zero `still_served` names the view and the exact key, which is the failure part (2)'s `residual=0` cannot see (a key can be deleted from Redis and then re-served if anything re-materialized it before the source rows were gone).
